title: Liberal or Restrictive Transfusion Strategy in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
shortTitle: SAHARA: liberal transfusion did not establish neurologic benefit
authors: SAHARA Trial Investigators on behalf of the Canadian Critical Care Trials Group
summary: SAHARA randomized 742 critically ill adults with aneurysmal SAH and anemia to liberal or restrictive transfusion. Unfavorable 12-month neurologic outcomes occurred in 33.5% versus 37.7% (RR 0.88; 95% CI 0.72–1.09; P=.22). Adverse-event incidence was similar.
whyItMatters: Does not establish a benefit from routinely transfusing every anemic SAH patient at 10 g/dL. Coordinate thresholds with neurocritical care rather than extrapolating from other brain-injury populations.
limitations: The confidence interval includes clinically relevant benefit and does not prove equivalence. This critical-care strategy was not a trial of resuscitation for active hemorrhagic shock.
population: Critically ill adults with acute aneurysmal SAH and anemia at 23 centers.
intervention: Mandatory red-cell transfusion when hemoglobin was ≤10 g/dL.
comparator: Optional transfusion when hemoglobin was ≤8 g/dL.
findings: Primary outcome: 122/364 versus 136/361; 725 participants had outcome data.
Functional independence and quality-of-life measures did not clearly differ.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill: first-online date verified from the PubMed electronic publication record. Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. This is historical evidence, not a new 2026 publication.
